comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C23-C31 comparing cultured and embryonic PSM4 cells. Both evaluations find this comparison well-supported and identify it as central to demonstrating the cell-autonomous program with extrinsic modulation. Peer reviewers highlight this as the 'main novelty' of the work.
Perfect agreement on claims C98-C101 validating the Mesp-ba-mKate2 transgenic reporter. Both evaluations accept this methodological validation as supporting the main findings without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C15-C22 demonstrating cell-autonomous oscillatory dynamics in isolated cells. OpenEval emphasizes the systematic experimental controls; peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing support' using 'thorough and quantitative single-cell real-time imaging.' Both find this central to the study's novelty. Peer review also includes C2 and C35 in their evaluation.

Strong agreement on claims C41-C44 from her1/her7 mutant experiments demonstrating clock-independent timer. OpenEval notes the evidence is strong but sample size not explicitly reported; peer reviewers accept without challenge as supporting the broader cell-autonomous timer conclusion. Peer review also includes C95 in their evaluation.

Agreement on claims C58-C61 characterizing FGF effects on oscillatory dynamics. Both evaluations accept these observations as supporting details within the FGF experiments, showing that FGF extends duration while preserving basic dynamics.

Agreement on claims C36-C40 regarding in vivo dynamics of clock arrest and differentiation timing. OpenEval emphasizes the loosened temporal coupling in culture versus embryos; peer reviewers accept this as part of the 'detailed description of the oscillatory system' without challenge.

Agreement on claims C81-C83 regarding uncoupling phenomenon. OpenEval explicitly marks this as UNCERTAIN, noting the observation is supported but mechanistic interpretations are speculative; peer reviewers accept without challenge, treating it as a minor observation within FGF experiments.

Agreement on claims C89-C94 regarding speculative molecular mechanisms. OpenEval marks this as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses requiring validation; peer reviewers accept these as possibilities for future investigation consistent with main findings. Peer review also includes C84, C96, C97 in their evaluation.

Agreement on claims C1, C7-C14 summarizing prior work and identifying the research gap. Both evaluations accept the literature review as appropriate and well-supported by citations. Peer review also includes C47-C49, C69, C74, C78-C79 in their evaluation of background statements.

Partial overlap on anteroposterior gradient experiments. OpenEval focuses on claims C64-C68 showing timer progression and TB/PSM4 arrest timing; peer reviewers group these with C70-C73 (TB tracking) and accept all as supporting the cell-autonomous timer concept without challenge.

Partial overlap on TB tracking experiments. OpenEval focuses on claims C70-C73 showing slowing initiates at TB exit; peer reviewers group these with C64-C68 (anteroposterior gradient) and accept all as supporting the timer initiation model.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C2, C3, C5, C6, C75-C77, C80). OpenEval synthesizes all experimental findings supporting the conceptual advance; peer reviewers accept the 'internal timer' proposal and the interplay between intrinsic program and external information. Peer review also includes C45, C46, C85, C86 in their evaluation.

Partial overlap on FGF experiments. OpenEval focuses on claims C50-C54, C57 showing FGF extends duration while maintaining temporal associations; peer reviewers group these with C62, C63, C87 and accept FGF as modulating the intrinsic program without challenge.

Agreement on claims C55-C56 regarding rare uncoupling phenotype. OpenEval notes this is an interesting observation requiring follow-up with limited interpretation due to small sample size; peer reviewers accept without challenge as a minor observation.

Partial overlap on in vivo reference patterns. OpenEval focuses on claims C32-C35 establishing arrest confinement to S-1; peer reviewers group these with C36-C40 (Mesp timing) as part of the detailed in vivo characterization.

Minimal overlap on FGF effects. OpenEval includes claims C53-C54 (coordination between clock arrest and differentiation) in broader FGF analysis; peer reviewers evaluate these claims separately as supporting details within accepted FGF experiments.

Minimal overlap on extrinsic signal roles. OpenEval focuses on claims C85-C88 synthesizing culture-embryo comparisons and FGF experiments; peer reviewers separately evaluate C88 (FGF insufficient for precision) as an accepted inference about additional signals.

Minimal overlap on synthesis claims. OpenEval focuses on claims C45-C46 synthesizing culture-embryo findings; peer reviewers include these in broader evaluation of main conclusions about intrinsic program and external information.

Minimal overlap on historical context. OpenEval focuses on claims C78-C79 contextualizing findings within Clock and Wavefront model; peer reviewers include these in broader evaluation of background statements and established knowledge.

Minimal overlap on control analysis. OpenEval includes claim C21 (survival time independence) in broader cell-autonomous demonstration; peer reviewers evaluate this separately as supporting cell-autonomous variability interpretation.

Minimal overlap on FGF dynamics. OpenEval includes claims C62-C63 (FGF preserves basic dynamics with disorganization) in broader FGF characterization; peer reviewers include these in overall acceptance of FGF modulation evidence.

Minimal overlap on extrinsic signal interpretation. OpenEval includes claim C87 (FGF role) in synthesis of extrinsic signal roles; peer reviewers include this in broader acceptance of FGF experiments.
Minimal overlap on in vivo patterns. OpenEval focuses on claims C32-C35 as in vivo reference; peer reviewers include C35 in broader evaluation of cell-autonomous dynamics demonstration.
Minimal overlap on main conclusions. OpenEval includes claim C2 in synthesis of all findings; peer reviewers include C2 in evaluation of cell-autonomous dynamics demonstration.
